Wearable EEG tasks: accuracy vs. channels × sampling rate × bit width

1 · Tasks

Each card is one downstream task: what it monitors, what is detected or which classes are told apart, and the public datasets used.

Target detection (visual ERP) →

Detection
Watches the brain’s reaction to symbols flashing on a screen and spots the rare target symbol.

Detects: the response to a target flash (‘OOO’, 1 in 5 flashes) versus a non-target flash (‘XXX’).

Classification3 classes

Classes:

  • box flickering at 8.57 Hz
  • box flickering at 12 Hz

2 · Models and methods

What each plot in section 3 means. A setting is one combination of number of electrodes, sampling rate and bit width.

Models

Official algorithm

The method the dataset’s own paper used (for example shrinkage LDA for ERP, CCA for SSVEP). We rerun it with the paper’s electrodes, windows and evaluation, so its numbers are comparable to the paper.

EEGNet

A small, widely used neural network for EEG. We use the same network for every task as a common reference, so differences between tasks are not caused by different models.

Training and inference methods

Retrain

A separate model is trained for every setting (every electrode set, sampling rate and bit width). This is the best a model can do at that setting, but switching settings on a device would need new training data with labels.

Bits at test

A model is trained for each electrode set and sampling rate on full-precision data. At test time the signal is stored with fewer bits. Shows what happens if only the ADC resolution is lowered and the model is not retrained.

Frozen + LS

One model is trained once at the full setting and then never changed. When electrodes are switched off, their signals are estimated from the remaining electrodes with a least-squares fit; lower sampling rates and bit widths are handled without retraining. No labels are needed.

Frozen + LS (one map)

Same frozen model as Frozen + LS, but the least-squares fill-in for switched-off electrodes is worked out only once, from full-rate, full-precision data, and then reused unchanged at every lower sampling rate and bit width. Nothing is re-fitted when the device changes its setting. No labels are needed.

Frozen + LS + BN

Same as Frozen + LS, plus one cheap adjustment: the network’s normalisation statistics are re-estimated on the new, unlabeled data.

Robust frozen

Like Frozen + LS, but during the one-time training the model sometimes sees filled-in electrodes instead of real ones, so it is used to them when electrodes are switched off later.

Robust frozen + BN

Robust frozen, plus the same unlabeled update of the normalisation statistics.

Elastic

One model trained once on many random settings (random electrode subsets, sampling rates and bit widths). At run time it is simply fed whatever setting the device is using.

Slimmable

An elastic model whose width can also be reduced (25–100% of its channels), trading a little accuracy for less computation.

Early exit

A network with extra outputs part-way through. If it is already confident after an early block it stops there, saving computation on easy inputs; the threshold sets how confident it must be.

3 · Accuracy surfaces

One panel per task; inside it, one block per dataset or electrode setup; inside each block, one plot per training / adaptation method. Pick any two of channels / Hz / bits as the x and y axes; the third is fixed by its buttons. Height = metric on a fixed 0–1 scale (mean over the tested channel subsets of that size; hover for the best subset). The red plane is the chance level of the task. Drag to rotate · scroll to zoom · double-click to enlarge. Switch a task to “Compare” to overlay any number of chosen plots (any dataset · model · method of that task) in one large cube, or show the difference of two.
